title: AI training companies
description: Companies that pay people to train and evaluate AI models: who they are, how they hire, how they pay, and what their live listings pay. Curated fields are checked against each company's own pages; see sources per record.

license.name: CC BY 4.0
license.attribution: Data from aitrainer.work/open-data/companies, licensed under CC BY 4.0 (creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0)

notes: Curated fields are null until checked against a primary source. Null means "not yet verified" or "the company does not publish it".
pay_observed_hourly_usd uses listings that state an hourly rate; estimates are excluded. Shown only with 10+ listings.

trustpilot_organic is the mean rating of organic (not company-invited) Trustpilot reviews from the aitrainer.work Trustpilot study (doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23018069), only for platforms with 30+ organic reviews. It is not Trustpilot's TrustScore.

companies.name: AfterQuery
companies.eligible_countries: 95 countries where Stripe pays out; 48 listed as unsupported, including Brazil, Nigeria, Egypt, Japan and China
companies.description: AfterQuery is an applied research lab that turns expert work into AI training data: fine-tuning examples, reasoning traces, grading rubrics, agent environments and computer-use demonstrations. It works with domain experts to capture how they reason through real tasks.
pros: Paid every Friday for the prior week's approved work
No fees from AfterQuery on payouts
Track every payout in Stripe or your Earnings dashboard
cons: Assessments are unpaid, and each pool's assessment can be taken once
There's no pass or fail notice; you hear back when a matching project comes up
Stripe is the only payout method, and the first payout has a 7-day hold

companies.name: Aligned Labs
companies.description: Aligned Labs, founded by ex-Google staff, matches PhDs and senior professionals to AI lab projects. You'll write novel training data, give RLHF feedback and evaluate model outputs in your field, and you set your own hourly rate.
pros: You set your own hourly rate
Applications are reviewed within 48 hours
Network of 20,000+ experts across 50+ research domains
cons: About page asks for 15+ years of experience or teaching certification
No pay figures published on the site

companies.name: Alignerr
companies.eligible_countries: Applicants from around the world who meet skill and communication requirements; visa holders only if their visa allows contract work
companies.description: Alignerr is Labelbox's contributor platform. You'll write code challenges, domain prompts and voice data, or grade model outputs against rubrics. Rates are listed on each project before you start, and the homepage says contributors are paid weekly.
pros: No minimum hours; the FAQ says many contributors work 20-25 hours a week
Pay is listed in each project description before you start
Homepage states contributors are paid weekly
cons: Identity check through Persona is required for all contributors
Some jobs add a Zara AI interview or a skills assessment
Every project starts with a calibration phase where sample work is reviewed

companies.name: Appen
companies.eligible_countries: 1M+ contributors across 170+ countries
companies.description: Appen is an ASX-listed data company founded in Sydney in 1996. Its contributor platform, CrowdGen, pays you to evaluate, annotate and write content for AI training, with expert projects in code, law, medicine, finance and linguistics.
pros: Pays via bank transfer, PayPal, Payoneer or Airtm
Rates are shown before you start
Contributors in 170+ countries and 235+ languages
cons: Rates vary by location and skills
Signup includes a verification step

companies.name: Atlas Capture
companies.eligible_countries: North America, Asia and Australia
companies.description: Atlas Capture pays you to record short videos of everyday tasks like cooking and cleaning on an iPhone app, used to train robotics models. There are also text labeling and AI feedback tasks in the browser, and every task shows its pay upfront.
pros: Paid biweekly with no minimum balance
No minimum hours or task quotas
Each task shows its pay before you start
cons: Recording tasks need an iPhone 11 or newer
Pay rates vary by region
Only available in North America, Asia and Australia

companies.name: BLEND
companies.eligible_countries: Freelancers in 172 countries
companies.description: BLEND, formerly One Hour Translation and now a Tasq.ai company, is a localization firm. Its freelancer portal takes translators and voice artists in 120+ languages, and it also sells AI training data annotation to clients.
pros: Separate applications for translators and voice artists
Work across 120+ languages
Freelancer community in 172 countries
cons: No pay rates or payment methods published on the freelancer page
Main site is aimed at business clients

companies.name: Claru
companies.eligible_countries: Most roles accept the US, Canada, Mexico and Brazil; capture variants also open in India, the Philippines, Indonesia, Vietnam, Argentina, Colombia, Chile and Peru
companies.description: Claru is Reka AI's data brand for physical and frontier AI. Contributors film first-person video of everyday tasks with gear Claru ships them, or do remote RLHF, annotation, code review and red teaming. Every listing shows its hourly rate in USD.
pros: Every listing shows its hourly rate in USD
Paid bi-weekly via Wise, Payoneer or bank transfer
Applications are reviewed within 3-5 business days
cons: Capture pay is set by region, from $5/hr in Asia to $15/hr in the US
Capture roles pay for accepted footage only
Camera equipment ships to you and goes back when the engagement ends

companies.name: Clickworker
companies.eligible_countries: Workers in 136 countries; you must be allowed to work where you live
companies.description: Clickworker is a German microtask platform where registered freelancers do data collection, labeling, categorization, surveys and app testing. It's paid per task at a fixed amount published before you start, with a weekly bill run.
pros: Weekly bill run, with PayPal payouts by Saturday
€10 minimum for PayPal and SEPA
Fixed pay per task, published in advance
cons: Payment methods depend on your country
Bank payouts take 5-7 business days after the bill run

companies.name: CloudFactory
companies.eligible_countries: Citizens of Nepal, Kenya, the Philippines or Colombia
companies.description: CloudFactory, founded in Nepal in 2010, hires Data Specialists for annotation, transcription, moderation and data extraction. You'll take a skills assessment and training, then get paid monthly into a local bank account.
pros: Paid monthly into your local bank account
Training provided before you start
Part-time and full-time options
cons: Only open to citizens of Nepal, Kenya, the Philippines or Colombia
Some projects run on scheduled shifts

companies.name: CNTXT AI
companies.description: CNTXT AI is an Arabic-first AI and data company in the UAE. Its careers page lists remote hourly contractor roles for AI training, such as biology evaluators and Python and C++ coding experts.
pros: Remote, hourly contractor roles
Listings for coding and science specialists
cons: Most of the site is aimed at enterprise clients
No pay rates or payment methods published

companies.name: DataAnnotation Tech
companies.description: DataAnnotation pays remote contractors to rank AI responses, check facts, label data and review subject-specific content. You get in by passing a one-hour Starter Assessment, and the FAQ says it pays through PayPal within a few days of a withdrawal request.
pros: Pay is sent via PayPal within a few days of each withdrawal request
Work on your own schedule with no long-term commitment
Coding and STEM projects are listed at $50-$100+/hr
cons: The Starter Assessment can only be taken once, with no retakes
The FAQ doesn't list which countries are eligible

companies.name: DATAmundi
companies.description: DATAmundi is the AI data and language brand of Summa Linguae Technologies, based in Kraków. Freelancers can register for data projects or localization work, including translation, editing, proofreading and QA.
pros: Separate registration for data projects and localization
Needs translators in technical, medical, legal and finance fields
cons: No pay rates or payment methods published
CAT tool knowledge recommended for translation work

companies.name: Ethos
companies.description: Ethos is an expert network run by Ethos Artificial Intelligence Limited in London. Its remote roles include creating and evaluating AI-generated work to help train an AI lab's language model, alongside paid consulting, advisory calls and market research.
pros: Free for experts to use
Featured opportunities list an hourly rate, e.g. $70/hr up to $1.4k/week
Rate and payment method are confirmed in writing before each project
cons: Ethos can require a third-party identity check before paying you
You can't take projects about an employer you worked for in the last six months

companies.name: Handshake
companies.eligible_countries: US-based with valid work authorization (F-1 students on CPT or OPT eligible, STEM OPT excluded)
companies.description: The Handshake AI Fellowship pays people with associate, bachelor's, master's or PhD backgrounds to evaluate and improve AI models remotely. It's run by the Handshake careers network, and payouts go out weekly through Stripe.
pros: Hourly pay of $40-$125 stated on the fellowship page
Payouts are sent by Wednesday for the previous Monday-Sunday week
No prior AI experience required
cons: Must be US-based with valid work authorization
Identity verification and a background check are part of onboarding

companies.name: iMerit
companies.description: iMerit, now part of EXL, provides annotation, model evaluation and fine-tuning data across image, video, LiDAR, text and audio. Individuals join through iMerit Scholars, a remote programme for domain experts in fields like law, medicine, finance and maths.
pros: Scholars work is remote and flexible
Projects run from days to long-term contracts
Scholars site lists fields from computer science and law to healthcare and humanities
cons: Scholars page doesn't publish pay rates
No classification or payment method details on the Scholars homepage

companies.name: Innodata
companies.description: Innodata is a Nasdaq-listed (INOD) data engineering company in Ridgefield Park, New Jersey. It sells data collection, annotation, fine-tuning data, RLHF and red teaming to AI builders, and hires through its own careers site.
pros: Publicly listed on Nasdaq as INOD
Says it has 11,500 in-house subject matter experts
cons: Careers page doesn't describe a contributor programme
No pay rates published on the careers homepage

companies.name: Invisible Technologies
companies.description: Invisible Technologies is an AI training and enterprise automation company. It recruits experts for data preparation, labeling and AI evaluation through its Meridial network, which it says holds 24,000+ vetted experts screened by skill, language and domain.
pros: Expert network screens by skill, language and domain
24,000+ vetted experts in the network
cons: Expert applications go through a separate site, meridial.ai
No pay rates on the main site

companies.name: Labela
companies.description: Labela pays medical, health, chemistry and biology experts to train AI on their own schedule. It's run by Lumos AI Research Corp., and contributors sign an independent contractor consulting agreement governed by Delaware law.
pros: Flexible schedule
Focused on medical and science expertise
cons: Contractor agreement: you handle your own taxes
Disputes settled by arbitration in Wilmington, Delaware

companies.name: Lilt
companies.description: LILT is an enterprise AI translation company founded in 2015. Its Horizon programme pays translators and linguists for labeling, transcription and evaluation tasks that train its multilingual models, and you'll get paid within 15 days of completing work.
pros: Paid within 15 days of completed work
Work from anywhere, choose your hours
cons: Aimed at professional translators and linguists
No rates published

companies.name: Lionbridge
companies.description: Lionbridge is a translation and localisation company with an AI training programme for freelancers. You'll pick projects in data collection, model evaluation, annotation, transcription or prompt writing, pass assessments, then work in its AuroraStudio platform.
pros: Freelance, you choose when and how much you work
Six task types, from annotation to prompt writing
cons: Each project needs an application and assessments
Rates and payment methods only shown after registering

companies.name: Luel
companies.description: Luel is a multimodal data lab that pays contributors to submit conversational audio, first-person videos and photos for AI training. Rates are set per task, for example $12/hr for American English conversations, and it claims 850,000+ contributors.
pros: Payouts processed daily
Posted rates per task, e.g. $12/hr for English conversations
Discord community for contributors
cons: Submissions are reviewed and can be rejected before payment
Rare-language audio pays $7.50/hr

companies.name: Mercor
companies.eligible_countries: 130+ countries via Stripe, plus Brazil, UAE, Nepal and Turkey via Wise; about 100 listed countries can't be onboarded
companies.description: Mercor hires professionals as contractors to train and evaluate AI models in fields like law, medicine and finance. Applicants do an AI interview and a one-time Persona ID check, and pay lands every Wednesday via Stripe or Wise.
pros: Paid every Wednesday for the previous work week
Homepage states an average contracted rate of $109/hr
Stripe Instant Payout gets funds to your bank in about 30 minutes for a 1% fee
cons: Includes an AI interview
Identity is verified once through Persona
Payout bank account must be in your own legal name

companies.name: Meridial (Invisible)
companies.description: Meridial is Invisible Technologies' marketplace for expert contractors. You'll write and rank model responses, red team, design rewards and validate agent trajectories. Each engagement lists its rate range up front, and earnings are paid every two weeks.
pros: Rate range is published on each engagement before you apply
Earnings are processed every two weeks
Work covers RLHF, SFT, red teaming and environment design
cons: You sign a Statement of Work before starting a project
Signing up includes a profile confirmation step

companies.name: Micro1
companies.eligible_countries: Global, except about 20 listed countries including China, Russia, Iran, Venezuela and Ukraine
companies.description: micro1 is a human data lab that trains and evaluates AI models. Experts in engineering, finance, healthcare, law and other fields apply, take an AI interview with its interviewer Zara, then join projects. Contracts and pay run through Deel.
pros: Paid in USD twice a month
Open to most countries worldwide
Process is apply, AI interview, onboard, start
cons: Includes an AI interview with an AI interviewer called Zara
Onboarding includes KYC identity verification
You sign a contractor agreement through Deel

companies.name: Mindrift
companies.eligible_countries: Global except 17 sanctioned countries and about 35 unsupported territories; 18+; some projects add their own requirements
companies.description: Mindrift is Toloka's platform for AI trainers. You'll write prompts, rate AI answers and rewrite them into ideal responses across 90+ domains and 20+ languages. It's freelance work with no fixed hours, paid on the 5th and 20th of each month.
pros: Paid twice a month, on the 5th and 20th
States $15-30/hr entry-level and $60-100+/hr for domain experts
No employment contract and no fixed hours
cons: Specialised projects need a CV, an assessment and ID verification
Not available in 17 sanctioned countries plus about 35 unsupported territories
Pay is set per project

companies.name: OneForma
companies.eligible_countries: 100+ countries
companies.description: OneForma is Centific's crowd platform for annotation, data collection, AI judging, transcription and translation projects. You create a profile, get matched to projects, and see the rate before you accept. It pays twice a month with no application fees.
pros: Paid twice a month, no minimum threshold, no fees
Rates shown before you accept a project
Available in 100+ countries
cons: Payout method must be connected before any production work
Project availability depends on matching

companies.name: Outlier AI
companies.eligible_countries: About 50 countries; the list is not published. Needs a valid ID and mobile number from your country of residence.
companies.description: Scale AI's freelance platform for AI training work. Contractors write prompts, build grading rubrics and rate model answers across coding, STEM and languages. Onboarding takes 30 to 90 minutes.
pros: Paid weekly, every Tuesday
You see the task rate before you start a project
Payout by PayPal, Airtm or ACH bank transfer
cons: Rates are not published before you sign up
You need an ID and phone number from your country of residence

companies.name: Pareto AI
companies.description: Pareto AI builds human training data for AI models. Its expert network takes specialists in medicine, law, STEM, finance, software and languages, who create challenges and domain insight for model training. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.
pros: Recruits across six fields, from medicine and law to software and linguistics
Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis
cons: Pay rates aren't published on the experts page
Payment methods and schedule aren't stated publicly

companies.name: Pasiflora AI
companies.description: Pasiflora AI connects credentialed specialists such as PhDs, MDs and JDs with companies training domain-specific models. Experts annotate, evaluate, write gold-standard answers and rank model outputs. You'll do a short voice assessment and a 30-minute training course before projects.
pros: States rates of $35 to $250 an hour depending on domain and task
No minimum time commitment; you accept or decline invitations
No per-task applications once approved
cons: Starts with a 3-question voice assessment and a qualification quiz
Most listings are interest lists for future projects
All task content is confidential

companies.name: Pila8
companies.description: Pila8 is a mobile app that pays you to record original human audio for AI training projects, from scripted prompts to conversations. Earnings post once a submission is approved, and pay is shown per opportunity.
pros: Short everyday audio tasks of 2 to 4 minutes pay $5 to $12
Longer qualified projects of 20+ minutes pay $50 or more
cons: Earnings only count once a submission is approved
Payment methods aren't listed on the info page

companies.name: Prolific
companies.eligible_countries: Residents of about 50 mostly OECD countries incl. US, UK, Canada, EU states, Australia, Japan, India, Brazil, Mexico, South Africa; 18+
companies.description: Prolific, founded at Oxford University in 2014, runs an online participant pool for academic research and AI developers. You'll take surveys, decision games and AI model evaluations. Researchers must pay at least £6 or $8 an hour.
pros: Researchers must pay at least £6/$8 per hour
Pays in real money via PayPal, with no points or gift cards
Instant PayPal transfers after your first 4 cashouts
cons: New participants join a waitlist before getting an invite
Minimum cashout is £6/$6
Only open to residents of listed countries

companies.name: Remotasks
companies.eligible_countries: 90+ countries
companies.description: Remotasks is Scale AI's tasking platform where you label images, transcribe audio and annotate data used to train AI. Harder task tiers pay more, and it reports 240,000+ taskers across 90+ countries.
pros: Taskers are paid weekly
Pays via PayPal or AirTM
Higher difficulty tiers pay more
cons: No pay rates published on the homepage

companies.name: Remo Experts
companies.eligible_countries: Global, with some projects limited by client or regulatory rules; basic English and a bachelor's degree required
companies.description: RemoExperts (REX) recruits subject-matter experts to train AI models, from coders and STEM PhDs to writers and video editors. It says it has 120K+ experts across 230+ domains. You'll take a 15-20 minute entry exam and verify your ID with Persona before applying to projects.
pros: Pays through Stripe, Payoneer or Wise
Covers 230+ domains, from coding to cinematography
Fully remote, with experts in 50+ countries
cons: Needs at least a bachelor's degree
Includes a 15-20 minute entry exam plus role-specific exams
ID verification through Persona

companies.name: Rise Data Labs
companies.eligible_countries: Experts worldwide; some roles limited to the US or to US, Canada and Europe
companies.description: Rise Data Labs supplies training and evaluation data for AI models using domain experts. You'll build work scenarios, write rubrics, grade AI outputs and spot reasoning errors. Most posted contract roles list $150 an hour.
pros: Weekly payouts with no minimums
Most posted roles list $150/hour
No AI experience needed if you're a domain expert
cons: Includes an AI or async interview and a domain skills test
Projects often expect 20 to 40 hours a week for about 2 weeks
Some roles are US-only

companies.name: RustLabs AI
companies.description: rustLabs is an applied AI lab that builds RL environments, evaluations and expert data for AI labs. Its expert network of 8,200+ professionals covers software, finance, ML, STEM, law and medicine. Pay runs $20 to $100+ an hour by field.
pros: States $20 to $100+ per hour, set by field and depth
Remote, self-scheduled work
Six fields open, including software, finance, legal and medical
cons: You apply with proof of expertise such as GitHub, papers or a portfolio
Includes a short calibration task in your field

companies.name: RWS (TrainAI)
companies.description: RWS runs the TrainAI community for freelance AI data work. You'll rate search results and ads, collect text, audio, image or video data, or annotate data. No experience is needed to join, and it's paid per task via PayPal or bank transfer.
pros: No experience needed to join
Paid per task via PayPal or bank account
Pay details are shared before each task
cons: Minimum age is 18
You supply your own computer and internet connection
Work comes as email invitations to projects you're matched to

companies.name: Scale AI
companies.description: Scale AI, founded in 2016 in San Francisco, provides training data, model evaluations and red-teaming for AI labs, enterprises and governments. It says it has paid $1B to contributors globally, who work through its platforms such as Remotasks.
pros: Reports $1B paid to contributors globally
Over 1,000 employees
cons: Contributor work runs through separate platforms, not scale.com
scale.com doesn't publish contributor pay rates

companies.name: Sigma AI
companies.eligible_countries: Varies by project; current listings target Latin America, India, North Africa and Europe
companies.description: Sigma AI, part of Sigma Group, supplies AI training data and evaluation for enterprise clients across 700+ languages. It hires remote contractors for language-specific annotation of speech, text, image and video data, posted on its careers site.
pros: Language-specific projects across 700+ languages and dialects
Listings are fully remote
cons: Pay isn't listed on the careers page
Projects are tied to specific languages and regions

companies.name: Silencio AI
companies.eligible_countries: 180+ countries
companies.description: Silencio runs a voice and audio data network for AI. Contributors record their own voice in their language, including low-resource languages, and are paid in stablecoin. It reports 2.5 million contributors across 180+ countries.
pros: Operates in 180+ countries
Focus on low-resource languages and dialects

Pay rates aren't published on the homepage

Paid exams show up as exam earnings
A human is involved in every final hiring decision

Some roles add a qualification exam or a call with the recruiting team

companies.name: Snorkel AI

Approved experts can start contributing the same day
Many projects pay for attempts plus performance bonuses

Pay is per project, with no hourly rate published

companies.name: Sovrano AI
companies.description: Sovrano AI is a Barcelona team that grew out of CareerOS, a 2024 student job startup. It connects graduates and domain experts with paid AI evaluation work such as RLHF ranking, multilingual evaluation, fact-checking and red-teaming. Current listings are paid internships.
pros: Free to join, sign up with email or Google
Work on your own schedule
Built on a network of 100+ university partners

Most listings are internships asking for a bachelor's or master's

companies.name: Stellar AI
companies.description: Stellar AI hires contractors to write tasks for AI agents, turn GitHub PRs into coding tasks and draft expert rubrics. It's hourly work with a stated base rate of $25 an hour, and you'll take a skill-match test before joining the annotator pool.
pros: States a base rate of $25 an hour
Pays weekly
No fixed schedule or minimum hours
cons: Needs a PayPal account to get paid
No set timeframe between joining the pool and a first project
Requires fluency in English

companies.name: Surge AI
companies.description: Surge AI supplies human data and RL environments to AI labs. Its consultant programme pays finance, accounting, healthcare ops and coding professionals to critique model answers and design test scenarios. You'll apply through its DataAnnotation platform.

Pays $100 for submitting an application and $100 more on acceptance
Work as much or as little as you like

Includes an assessment
